punchline: Memory champions generally don't have unusual brains; they use an ancient technique anyone can learn.
thirty_sec: Tony Buzan co-founded the World Memory Championships in 1991, where competitors memorize decks of cards and long strings of numbers. Most use the memory palace, placing vivid images along a familiar route, a technique going back to the legend of Simonides in ancient Greece. Brain-imaging research suggests champions don't generally have unusual brains, just trained strategies. Memory is a skill.
